description: 1307. Clinton to Haldimand. New York. Received letters announcing his arrival. No reinforcement asked for, but will send 2,000 men if the presence of the French fleet does not compel him to defer it. Johnson goes to Canada to arrange the Indian Department. Sends copy of letter addressed to Germain.

1910. Clinton to Haldimand. New York. Communicating in order to give all necessary information about the state of affairs in this part of the country. Encloses extracts of intelligence that have been received. With respect to his own situation, he is unable to act offensively.

1911. Clinton to Haldimand. New York. Has great hopes of redeeming the Army of Convention and Commissioners are now met at Amboy for the purpose of settling a general cartel. Establishment and erection of a fort on the Penobscot River with a detachment of 500 men. Rebels find difficulty in raising an army this year.

1938. [Clinton] to Haldimand. New York. Rebels mean to make attack upon Detroit this spring. They intend to make a [jaunt ?] on the Susquhannah in order to draw the attention of Colonel Butler and the Indians from the other quarter.
1744. Clinton to Haldimand warning him of impending rebel movements in his area and that rebel forces are likely to be led by Gates and Arnold.
1767. Clinton to Haldimand alerting him to intelligence received that rebels led by Arnold and Gates, are planning a serious attack in his area and putting him on his guard [in Canada].

2142. Clinton to Haldimand. New York. Clinton discussing how he will send 1500 to 2000 men to support Haldimand against the rebels in Canada, or as soon as he is able (or if the promised reinforcements arrive from England). Ends by revealing that this measure would be a severe blow on his future projects.

1828. Clinton to Haldimand referring to previous correspondence regarding the rebels building of a number of batteaux and other vessels. Pleased to report that intelligence now indicates that articifers employed on the work have been withdrawn indicating that the project for the invasion of Canada has been postponed, for now.
2380. Clinton to Haldimand. Letter in cypher.
2269. Clinton to Haldimand regarding negotiations for prisoner exchanges.
2270. Clinton to Haldimand recommending Captain Ridsdale of the 44th Foot.

2268. Clinton to Haldimand concerning Colonel de Loos of the [German] Regiment of Losebergh and recommending him in the strongest terms before his departure for Canada. His having already been esteemed as an officer of great merit by the King of Prussia [Frederick the Great] and the Duke of Brunswick.

2894. [Letter in cypher, no date or names however it was found by comparison to be the same as one at British Museum.] Clinton to Haldimand stating that information received indicates that a French force had sailed around 3 May with seven ships of the line and 20-25 transport vessels. Included with the fleet is an estimated 5,200 land force and they are heading for Canada. Admiral Arbuthnot will be reinforced in proportion. Further intelligence indicates that the force will assemble at Rhode Island before making its way eventually to St John's by the St Lawrence River.

2962. Clinton to Haldimand. New York. A message that reads, Monsieur Ternay arrived at Rhode Island with seven sail of the line, three frigates and about 5,000 troops who are said to be sickly. There is little probabililty of their attemting Canada this year, their principal efforts being intended against this place. Note that a large part of the despatch is encoded.

3138. Clinton to Haldimand. New York. Discusses how from intelligence lately received, there will be an attempt against Canada, which would render naval transactions on the coast improbable. A second addition mentions that because of the intention against Canada, realiance on the country for the delivery of supplies of flour and other provision could not be guaranteed. Suggesting taking from the inhabitants.

3077. Clinton to Haldimand. New York. Number 24. Concerned for the miscarriage of the Quebec Fleet, the greatest part of which has been taken by the French and [the American] rebels. Ternay's fleet blocked up at Rhode Island, with Rodney's presence the rebels have not attempted upon this place, and the English fleet with recruits and stores have arrived, but the Cork fleet have not. Also on the expedition of 3,000 men under Leslie, and an accommodation with Spain. The second letter written 9 November mentions the attempt against Canada, the carriage of armaments and the supply of provisions.

3050. Clinton to Haldimand. New York. General Arnold has given up the forts at West Point and joined Clinton which has thrown the rebel army into great confusion, Admiral Rodney in on the coast with a superior fleet, and there is little probability of a second division of French ships this year. Lord Cornwallis gained a complete victory on 16 August at Camden over the rebel army under General Gates, and there is a great defection in the Spanish Colonies. Document contains (3 sides of) coding.

3005. Clinton to Haldimand. New York. Monsieur Rochambeau and Monsieur Schifflin having both escaped imprisonment with the rebels, came to New York destitute. Clinton was induced to give them his warrant on the Deputy Paymaster General for 100 guineas each. He therefore begs that directions to the Paymaster in Canada to stop this sum in his hands and surcharge himself with the amount in his account with the Paymaster General. These men take the present opportunity of returning to Canada.

3660. [Clinton] to Haldimand. New York. Informing that General Riedesel has sailed for Canada with a considerable number of officers and men. The French and rebels only wait for a reinforcement from the West Indies to make an attack upon this post, which he thinks they will certainly attempt and is hourly expected. The enemy's force is about 4,000 French and 7,000 rebels.

3636. Clinton to Haldimand. New York. Mentions letters fowarded by Ensigns Drummond and Prentice which Clinton says he has not received. Discussion including the reunion of Vermont with the mother country, Riedesel and a number of officers and men going in convoy to Halifax and Quebec, and the two large victualling transports.
3537. Henry Clinton [?] to Haldimand, [two letters one in code.] An earlier letter relates to supplies for German troops in Canada and the need for the early departure of a convoy to supply them.

3502. Clinton to Haldimand. New York. Seven pages of coding plus two separate letters of the same date. The first discusses the status of Vermont in relation to Ethan Allen, and events concerning the interception of letters. The second, the exchange of officers, the application for a ship of war, the sending of newspapers, and enclosure of an account of monies which have been paid.
3811. [Clinton to Haldimand]. New York. [A letter, no names, supposed to be Clinton and Haldimand, acknowledging receipt of earlier letters and commenting that Cornwallis' situation is alarming].
4152. Clinton to Haldimand. Cypher letter.
4216. Clinton to Haldimand. In Cipher (second letter deciphred, regarding the position of the 'Vermonters').
